title: A Composition Design Strategy for Refractory High-Entropy Alloys.

recollection.starting_material: guess: elemental powders of refractory metals (e.g., Nb, Mo, Ta, W, V)
recollection.intervention: guess: a computational composition‐screening strategy combining CALPHAD thermodynamic predictions with atomic‐size and valence‐electron‐concentration criteria, followed by arc‐melting and homogenization
recollection.structure: guess: single‐phase body‐centered‐cubic (BCC) solid solutions with high configurational entropy
recollection.mechanism: guess: stabilization of the BCC phase by high mixing entropy and suppression of intermetallic formation by atomic‐size misfit and favorable enthalpy of mixing, leading to lattice‐distortion and solid‐solution strengthening
recollection.results: guess: identification of optimal compositions exhibiting yield strengths above 1 GPa at room temperature and retaining >800 MPa at 800 °C, microhardness around 400 HV, and creep‐resistance strain rates <10^–5 s^–1 at 1000 °C under 100 MPa

score.note: The recollection partially captures computational composition screening using VEC and subsequent arc melting, but incorrectly adds CALPHAD, atomic-size criteria, and homogenization while omitting the modulus-based screening details and selected composition. Single-phase BCC structure is correct. The proposed entropy/lattice-distortion strengthening mechanism does not match the paper’s VEC–Peierls barrier–dislocation mobility mechanism. Yield strength above 1 GPa and roughly 400 HV hardness are close, but the central 35.7% fracture strain and 2550 MPa compressive strength are omitted, while high-temperature strength and creep claims are unsupported.
